papers_read.title_as_printed: Development and validation of a machine learning model for early screening of high-risk mild cognitive impairment from the multi-cohort data (Wu et al., International Journal of Medical Informatics 203 (2025) 106030)
A prediction model for the risk of developing mild cognitive impairment in older adults with sarcopenia: evidence from the CHARLS (Liu et al., Aging Clinical and Experimental Research (2025) 37:69)

what_each_reports.P-96: Cross-sectional screening for currently present MMSE-defined cognitive impairment (>=1 SD below the age-stratum mean MMSE, AACD criterion) in the general CHARLS 2015 older population (n=2,932, 17.7% impaired), random forest on 7 routine variables (education, grip strength, height, weight, creatinine, MCV, platelets), stratified 5-fold CV: AUROC 0.93 (95% CI 0.91-0.95) on the training set; external AUROC 0.83 (Yiwu 2021) and 0.87 (CHARLS 2011).
what_each_reports.P-166: Prognostic prediction of INCIDENT MCI over the next four years among CHARLS participants with sarcopenia (AWGS 2019) and normal cognition at baseline (HRS-style 21-point cognition, AACD plus no IADL disability), 4-layer feed-forward network on 8 sarcopenia-related variables: test AUC 0.708 (95% CI 0.544-0.844, n~83); temporal validation (CHARLS 2015-2018, n=156, 25 events) AUC 0.711 (0.588-0.823).

quantity_a: Diagnostic (cross-sectional) ROC-AUC for currently present MMSE-defined cognitive impairment vs not, general Chinese older population (CHARLS 2015), 7 routine physical/blood variables, internal CV
quantity_b: Prognostic ROC-AUC for developing MCI within four years among cognitively normal older adults with sarcopenia (CHARLS 2011-2015, validated 2015-2018), 8 sarcopenia-related variables, held-out test and temporal validation
incompatible_if_same: If the quantities were the same the intervals would not overlap (0.91-0.95 vs 0.544-0.844 and 0.588-0.823), but they are not the same quantity: one is detection of prevalent impairment in the general population, the other prediction of incident MCI over four years in a sarcopenic, cognitively normal subgroup with a different cognitive instrument and case definition.

gates.task: mismatch: P-96 is cross-sectional detection (T1); P-166 predicts incident MCI over four years (the registry codes it T2). The record's task_equal='Yes' and 'AUC 0.711 on T1' are wrong; no waiver on record
gates.dataset_family: match: both CHARLS (overlapping waves 2011 and 2015), which also makes the pair non-independent
gates.validation_tier: mismatch: P-96 reports external geographic and temporal validation (registry V4) but the contested 0.93 is its internal training-set figure; P-166 reports a temporal validation within CHARLS (registry V3)
gates.modality_family: match: clinical/tabular (physical examination, anthropometric and questionnaire variables)

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: same metric type (ROC-AUC) but different endpoints (prevalent MMSE-based impairment vs incident MCI within four years defined from HRS-style cognition plus IADL), different horizon (none vs four years) and different population behind the label (general older adults vs sarcopenic, baseline-normal older adults)
performance_validity: flag does not apply: neither paper is flagged; P-96's 0.93 is below 0.97 and comes from a cohort of 2,932 with external validation
independence: Shared cohort: both draw on CHARLS, including the 2011 and 2015 waves, so participants may overlap; recorded as non-independence. Different author groups (Zhejiang University vs Nanjing Medical University).
grounds: P-96's AUROC 0.93 is for detecting currently present MMSE-defined impairment in the general CHARLS 2015 population, a cross-sectional diagnostic quantity.
P-166's AUC 0.711 is for predicting MCI incidence over the next four years among cognitively normal sarcopenic participants, a prognostic quantity with a four-year horizon.

The population behind the label differs (general older adults vs a sarcopenia subgroup) and the cognitive case definitions differ (MMSE vs a 21-point HRS battery plus IADL), so the task gate fails with no waiver on record.
The CHARLS overlap is recorded as non-independence; it does not make the quantities the same.

evidence_quotes.quote: Data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) 2015 were used to develop the model.
Of the five machine learning algorithms assessed, the RF model showed the best performance, with an AUROC of 0.93[95 %CI, 0.91–0.95]
Third, the cross-sectional design of this study limits the ability to infer causal relationships and to track the progression of MCI over time.
Our model forecasts MCI incidence over the next four years, categorizing patients into low and high-risk groups based on their risk levels.
Only longitudinal data with normal cognitive function at baseline measurement and with indicators of cognitive and activities of daily living (ADL) outcomes were included.
The AUC of the validation centralized model was 0.711 (0.95 CI, 0.588–0.823).

record_defects: claim_b 'P-166: AUC 0.711 on T1' is wrong on task: P-166 predicts four-year incident MCI (the registry itself codes it T2).
task_equal='Yes' is wrong: cross-sectional detection vs four-year incidence prediction.

resolution_note says 'Confirmed genuine: Same metric type (AUC)' while resolution says 'Rejected - false positive'; the note is internally inconsistent and the same metric type does not make the endpoints the same.
P-96's 0.93 is its training-set (internal CV) figure; the record does not state that its external AUROCs are 0.83 and 0.87.
what_would_change_the_verdict: A pair of CHARLS studies reporting AUCs for the same endpoint (e.g. both prevalent MMSE-based impairment in the general population, or both four-year incident MCI) with non-overlapping intervals.
